projects.name: 1.1.1.4 - Support introduction of key technologies along the value chains of targeted crops (such as rice, cassava, cocoa, coffee, Cashew) livestock , fishery and vegetables.
projects.description:
The ILO with funding from the EU through the Opportunity Salone Programme piloted a total of seven interventions; three in the cassava value chain, two in vegetables value chain and two in palm oil value chain in Port Loko, Bombali, Kenema and Bo districts to help SME partners and farmers improve their productivity and develop new products through the use of improved technologies. For example: 
1. Imam Moiwo Palm Oil Plantation was supported to use improved palm oil processing presser to produce high quality palm oil. This improved presser machine is able to squeeze more oil palm from the fruit thereby increasing palm oil production by over 30%.  
2. SEDMO Construction, Agriculture and General Services was encouraged to invest in the processing of palm kernel oil by collecting and processing the kernel nut, which is usually considered as waste after the extraction of palm oil. Entering into cost-sharing partnership arrangement with the Opportunity Salone Programme, SEDMO upgraded its processing machines and equipment to improved/ mechanised palm kernel cracker and processing machines, significantly increasing both the quality and quantity of palm kernel oil production. 
3. Bokatala Limited provides market linkage by buying and selling onion from groups of farmers in Lungi, Port Loko District. Over the years, they suffered huge losses due to poor storage and processing facilities, causing spoilage and often force them to auction their onion below market prices. Through the Opportunity Salone Programme, ILO supported Bokatala to establish an onion processing and storage facility that is equipped with a solar system. With this facility, Bokatala is able to process and preserve onion for longer periods before supplying the market. This has greatly reduced losses and offers Bokatala the leverage to barging better price for their onion.
projects.outcome: Output 1.1.1 - Farmers especially women, youth and other vulnerable groups to have equal access to information and decision-making opportunities on land tenure, knowledge of improved agricultural practices, inputs, technology, financial services, linkage to markets, leveraging appropriate technologies and innovations

projects.name: 3.1.3.1 - Support to review, update, and development of laws, policies, strategies, guidelines and tools that improve access, quality and patient safety toward achieving UHC
projects.description:
The team sustained its prioritization of the creation of an enabling policy and legislative environment for the attainment of the three transformative results in Sierra Leone. Following the enactment of the Gender Equality and Women’s Empowerment Act in January 2023, UN Agencies supported the Government in the rolling out of an implementation plan for the enforcement of the Act, which included building and strengthening the capacity of line ministries that are central to the implementation of the Act.

Further, four national strategies aimed at advancing reproductive health were developed; these are the RMNCAH Extended strategy, Supply Chain Strategy, the National Fistula Strategy and the National Strategic Policy on elimination of cervical cancer and accompanying Clinical Guidelines. A review of the National Strategy for the reduction of teenage pregnancy and child marriage was also undertaken to inform the formulation of the next strategy. UN also supported the launch of Sierra Leone’s rights-based family planning commitments made through the FP2030 partnership. Additionally, in partnership with the Ministry of Health, the Midwifery Census was undertaken which is expected to guide interventions and policy decision towards strengthening the Midwifery health work force in Sierra Leone.
projects.outcome: Output 3.1.3 - The population has access to integrated people-centred health services to achieve Universal Health Coverage (UHC)

projects.name: 1.1.1.8 - Build the capacity of youth and young women in agricultural production and value addition, through vocational skills and linking them to employment with agro-processing companies
projects.description:
Adamaris gari processing industry in Makeni, Bombali District received support to produce high value cassava flour for the backery industry. The enterprise worked with about 75 outgrower cassava farmer groups by providing them with tillage services, extension services, necessary farm inputs and ready market for their harvest. The outgrower farmers in turn supplied Adamaris with cassava, which is the main raw material used in the production of cassava flour. These farmers have since received entrepreneurship training from training of trainers (TOT) business coaches trained by Opportunity Salone to help them treat farming as a business. Staff of Adamaris have received training on occupational Safety and health in the workplace and productivity improvement. In addition, the factory has undergone a major upgrade to improve its capacity to produce more.
In addition, ILO conducted several capacity building workshops/ training programmes for district council staff, SME contractors, SME business enterises and rural women, youths amd persons with disabilities. These trainings include the Start and Improve Your Business (SIYB), Financial Literacy and MYCOP. In addition, ILO sponsored exchange visits through which government officials, including the Minister of Works and Public Assets, staff of Public-private Unit under the Vice President's Office, and SLRA visited other countries to learn about feeder road maintenence mechanisms that uses sustainable public-private financing.

projects.name: 1.1.1.4 - Support introduction of key technologies along the value chains of targeted crops (such as rice, cassava, cocoa, coffee, Cashew) livestock , fishery and vegetables.
projects.description:
The ILO with funding from the EU through the Opportunity Salone Programme piloted a total of seven interventions; three in the cassava value chain, two in vegetables value chain and two in palm oil value chain in Port Loko, Bombali, Kenema and Bo districts to help SME partners and farmers improve their productivity and develop new products through the use of improved technologies. For example: 
1. Imam Moiwo Palm Oil Plantation was supported to use improved palm oil processing presser to produce high quality palm oil. This improved presser machine is able to squeeze more oil palm from the fruit thereby increasing palm oil production by over 30%.  
2. SEDMO Construction, Agriculture and General Services was encouraged to invest in the processing of palm kernel oil by collecting and processing the kernel nut, which is usually considered as waste after the extraction of palm oil. Entering into cost-sharing partnership arrangement with the Opportunity Salone Programme, SEDMO upgraded its processing machines and equipment to improved/ mechanised palm kernel cracker and processing machines, significantly increasing both the quality and quantity of palm kernel oil production. 
3. Bokatala Limited provides market linkage by buying and selling onion from groups of farmers in Lungi, Port Loko District. Over the years, they suffered huge losses due to poor storage and processing facilities, causing spoilage and often force them to auction their onion below market prices. Through the Opportunity Salone Programme, ILO supported Bokatala to establish an onion processing and storage facility that is equipped with a solar system. With this facility, Bokatala is able to process and preserve onion for longer periods before supplying the market. This has greatly reduced losses and offers Bokatala the leverage to barging better price for their onion.

projects.description: ILO through the Opportunity Salone Programme with funding from the EU undertook feeder road maintenance work during the first quarter of 2023 in Bo, Kenema, Port Loko and Bombali district mainly to improve on farmers' access to the market for their products. Through this intervention, local communities who supplied labour were trained on feeder road maintenance, OSH and paid daily wage, thereby creating alternative livelihood and employment opportunities for them

projects.name: 3.1.3.1 - Support to review, update, and development of laws, policies, strategies, guidelines and tools that improve access, quality and patient safety toward achieving UHC
projects.description:
The team sustained its prioritization of the creation of an enabling policy and legislative environment for the attainment of the three transformative results in Sierra Leone. Following the enactment of the Gender Equality and Women’s Empowerment Act in January 2023, UN Agencies supported the Government in the rolling out of an implementation plan for the enforcement of the Act, which included building and strengthening the capacity of line ministries that are central to the implementation of the Act.

Further, four national strategies aimed at advancing reproductive health were developed; these are the RMNCAH Extended strategy, Supply Chain Strategy, the National Fistula Strategy and the National Strategic Policy on elimination of cervical cancer and accompanying Clinical Guidelines. A review of the National Strategy for the reduction of teenage pregnancy and child marriage was also undertaken to inform the formulation of the next strategy. UN also supported the launch of Sierra Leone’s rights-based family planning commitments made through the FP2030 partnership. Additionally, in partnership with the Ministry of Health, the Midwifery Census was undertaken which is expected to guide interventions and policy decision towards strengthening the Midwifery health work force in Sierra Leone.
projects.outcome: Output 3.1.3 - The population has access to integrated people-centred health services to achieve Universal Health Coverage (UHC)

framework.name: Strategic Priority 4 - Protection and Empowerment of the Most Vulnerable
framework.description:
6264 entrepreneurs, (92% women), have been trained on financial literacy and have benefited from business development skills training, business coaching/mentorship, and access to finance, all aimed improving business and economic opportunities for the women entrepreneurs and their households.  
2975 of the entrepreneurs trained are linked to finance services and more than 828 have benefited from loans to grow their businesses. 314 have had their businesses formalized.
